eventMetadata.context_description: **Ongoing southwest monsoon activity across the Philippines is the dominant factor anchoring trader expectations for Manila's highest temperature on August 14, 2026, near the seasonal norm of 30–32 °C.** Official PAGASA forecasts for Metro Manila show a daytime high of 31–33 °C with lows around 25–26 °C and a 90 % chance of rain or thundershowers, while international models (AccuWeather, timeanddate) converge on 30–31 °C maxima under overcast skies and scattered convection. Persistent cloud cover and moisture from the monsoon suppress daytime heating, preventing excursions above 33 °C or sharp drops below 30 °C that would require atypical clear, calm conditions. With the market date only hours away, short-range model runs exhibit limited spread, producing the observed clustering around 31 °C (44.5 % implied probability) and 32 °C (28.5 %), with lower-probability tails for 30 °C or 33 °C reflecting residual forecast uncertainty in rainfall timing and intensity. No major tropical cyclone or anomalous ridge is projected to alter steering patterns or insolation before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Official Met Office guidance for London on August 14, 2026, forecasts a sunny maximum of 32°C with only a 10% rain chance, following Thursday’s peak near 35°C amid an ongoing amber extreme-heat warning.** This positions the 32–34°C outcomes (collectively ~92% implied probability) as the consensus range, reflecting model consensus on modest cooling from a weakening high-pressure setup and southerly flow. Ensemble runs and historical late-summer anticyclonic patterns support limited further intensification, while urban heat-island effects at stations such as London City Airport or Heathrow introduce minor upward bias that traders appear to price into the 33°C lead. Recent model adjustments and the broader record-warm 2026 summer context reinforce tight clustering around these thresholds ahead of final observations.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Warsaw Chopin Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Warsaw Chopin Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pl/warsaw/EPWA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and Global Forecast System show broad consensus for a daytime maximum near 26°C in Warsaw on August 14, supported by southerly advection of warmer continental air under building high pressure and mostly clear skies. Ensemble spreads remain modest, with limited divergence on exact peak values, while overnight lows near 14–16°C further constrain the diurnal range. Updated short-range runs and surface observations through August 13 continue to reinforce this central tendency ahead of final verification.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple meteorological models converge on a daytime high near 17–18°C in Moscow for August 14, with modest spread arising from differences in predicted cloud cover, boundary-layer mixing, and weak northerly advection of cooler maritime air. Persistent light cloud and moderate northwesterly winds are expected to limit surface heating compared with clearer August climatology, while any breaks in cloud or slightly stronger insolation could push the maximum 1–2°C higher; conversely, increased low-level moisture or earlier precipitation would cap it near 16°C. This narrow range of plausible outcomes—driven by short-range model variability in radiative and advective processes rather than large-scale synoptic shifts—explains why trader probabilities cluster tightly around the 17°C and 18°C bins, with lower odds assigned to outliers beyond 19°C or below 16°C.

Historical August maxima frequently reach 34–36°C, and current model consensus shows limited spread, aligning with the market’s closely matched probabilities across the 32–36°C range. Updated CWA guidance and short-range model runs over the next 48 hours will likely refine the outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader sentiment remains closely split** on Chongqing's August 15 peak temperature because short-range numerical weather prediction models show notable spread around the typical mid-August subtropical high of 34–36 °C. Regional high pressure favoring clear skies and strong solar heating competes with possible monsoon moisture intrusions that could increase cloud cover, trigger convection, and cap daytime maxima near or below 32 °C. Chongqing’s enclosed Sichuan Basin topography and urban heat-island effect amplify sensitivity to small changes in boundary-layer moisture and wind, while historical climatology records occasional 40–42 °C spikes when subsidence strengthens. Fresh CMA and ECMWF runs expected within 24–48 hours represent the next high-impact data releases that could narrow the 50 %–49.5 % market-implied odds between the 42 °C+ and 32 °C-or-below outcomes.
